main_text.p: rabili prœda à Germanis & Hispanis militibus sa-ta[?], Pontifex ipse multis probris adfectus, in eorū incidit manus. Inde Germanorum ecclesias maiores, Papatum uelut Antichristi regnum uerbo sanguinē[?] detestatas, amisit. Subinde tamen astutus & audax lupus iam potentissimis regum populorumq; retibus instructus, Christi oues Lutherismi praetextu ad necem uenaturus, mense septembri anno Domini 1534. insulito[?] ueneficio, nempe funalis fumo, cum aliquot Cardinalium & amicis fa-miliaribus, in acerbae necis retia incidit. De hoc Clemente sic habet Vulteius:

De Clemente, quod est conscriptu cirmine crimen,
Id uerum, aut falsum protinus esse scio.

Si uerum est, uerè iam possum dicere, mundi
Vrna breuis uitium claudit, & anne scelus.

Si falsum est, uerè iam possum scribere, mundi
Dux, pax, lux, paruo contegitur tumulo.

At falsum esse reor. Quis enim committere summū
Pontificem Romæ talia monstra putet?

Ex Commentarijs Ioannis Fuccij, & quorundam aliorum: Anno Domini 152[?] Clemens septimus Rom. pontifex, sed olim Hierosolymitanus miles, et Prior Capuensis, Hadriano quinto successit, cui Iulius antea nomē erat, quod & in Papatu fernare decreuerat. Sed Cardinalium monitu, Clementis

page.notes: Printed text runs to the foot of the page with the catchword "mentis" at the bottom right. A small stray mark (ı) lies at the far left of the bottom line; not printed text, left out. Underlining in the text (under "insulito ueneficio", "Vulteius", "Hadriano quinto successit") is ink marking, not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "ta[?]" at the line end after "sa-" (the word is partly obscured); "insulito[?]"; "sanguinē[?]"; "152[?]" (the numeral is cut off at the line end, probably 1523 or 1527, set as printed); the first line is slightly faded at its left edge. Verse lines are printed as run-in lines with breaks; left as they stand. The left edge shows a fragment of the neighbouring page, left out.
